steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Food labels are legally required to provide: name of the food, ingredients list (in descending order of weight), allergen information, net quantity, use-by or best-before date, storage instructions, and name/address of the manufacturer. | Key Fact: The traffic light labelling system uses colour coding: green (low — healthier choice), amber (moderate), red (high — eat in smaller amounts or less often) for fat, saturated fat, sugars, and salt. | Key Fact: Use-by dates are about safety: food should NOT be eaten after its use-by date, even if it looks and smells fine (particularly for high-risk foods like meat and dairy). | Key Fact: Best-before dates are about quality: food is at its best before this date but is usually still safe to eat afterwards (e.g. dried pasta, tinned goods).

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on key terms from food labelling & marketing, and one past-paper question.
